name: Bauhaus
label: 4AD
lede: Four art-school and factory kids from Northampton cut a nine-minute single about a dead horror actor six weeks after they started, and goth historians still call it the genre's first record. They quit at the top in 1983, then kept coming back, once upside down.

eras.title: Six weeks to nine minutes
eras.text: Daniel Ash wanted a singer who looked the part and found an old school friend working at a printing factory. Within weeks they had a name borrowed from a German art school, a bass player's younger brother on drums, and the record that started goth.

years.src: Wikipedia: Daniel Ash · Wikipedia: Peter Murphy
years.h: Peter Murphy's first rehearsal: Ash plays blues, Murphy sings the newspaper
years.p: [[Daniel Ash|d4aa1162-78ac-437f-9900-97460e4e2f34]] looks up [[Peter Murphy|b78346af-e3ce-4b36-a0d5-032414de8a27]], a schoolfriend now working at a local printing firm. At the first try-out, Ash plays a 12-bar blues while Murphy sings newspaper articles over it.
years.xp: Murphy had left school at 16 to work at a family printing business, first as a bookbinder, then as a printer, while he painted and wrote on the side. Ash had gone to art school. Both were born in Northampton in 1957.

years.h: Bauhaus 1919 loses its bassist and half its name
years.p: [[Kevin Haskins|476cc87e-9665-43bb-80ea-7e123390ac64]] is on drums and Chris Barber on bass. Within weeks Barber is gone and Haskins's older brother [[David J|41225e9f-3b4c-4287-a778-165c65f04be9]] takes over, shortening the name to Bauhaus.

years.h: First gig: New Year's Eve at the Cromwell pub, Wellingborough
years.p: Bauhaus plays its first show on the last night of 1978, in Murphy's home town.

q: Bela was our interpretation of dub.
years.src: Wikipedia: Bela Lugosi · Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Uncut
years.h: 'Bela Lugosi's Dead' runs 9:36, and Murphy waits nearly three minutes to come in
years.p: Recorded in one six-hour session at Beck Studios in Wellingborough on January 26, six weeks into the band's life, and released on Small Wonder as a 12-inch, first pressed on white vinyl. It misses the main chart but sits on the indie lists for over two years.
years.xp:
Murphy had a cold and had never sung into a studio microphone before. Haskins played a bossa nova beat; Ash got the sound from partial barre chords with the top E and B strings left open. David J wrote the words, about Lugosi's funeral, and Murphy said later the horror trappings were meant with a sense of humour.

Goth historians now call it the first true record in the genre. Rolling Stone ranked it No. 60 among the 100 greatest debut singles.

Engineer Derek Tompkins ran the session, which cost the band 11 pounds and produced four songs; 'Bela' was a first take. Small Wonder's Pete Stennett didn't mind the length: 'I didn't give a fuck how long it was.' When John Peel played it, the BBC switchboard jammed with people asking to hear it again, and a Peel session followed. Murphy's later verdict: 'It was the Stairway to Heaven of the 1980s.'

eras.title: Out of the 4AD gate
eras.text: Small Wonder couldn't fund a tour, so Bauhaus went to a Beggars Banquet offshoot that had just changed its name from Axis to 4AD. In one year they gave the new label three singles and its first No. 1 indie album, crossed the Atlantic, and graduated to the parent label, the only band ever to follow that plan.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: In the Flat Field · Wikipedia: 4AD
years.h: 'Dark Entries' is the band's first record on 4AD
years.p: They leave Small Wonder for lack of touring support. The song comes out of The Picture of Dorian Gray, Murphy's favourite novel.
years.xp: [[Ivo Watts-Russell|cf86cec1-1baf-4d8a-ba1e-01568332585a]] and Peter Kent had started the label as Axis Records under Beggars Banquet on November 12, 1979. Someone else owned 'Axis', so after four singles it became 4AD, short for 'forward'.

years.h: 'Terror Couple Kill Colonel' follows on 4AD
years.p: The band's second single for the label, and third overall.

years.h: Bauhaus crosses the Atlantic for Toronto, Chicago and New York
years.p: In September they play Space Place in Chicago, a show booked by the owners of Wax Trax! Records.

years.h: NME hates In the Flat Field; it tops the indie chart anyway
years.p: The self-produced debut, cut at BBC Maida Vale and Southern Studios, reaches No. 1 on the UK independent chart and No. 72 on the main chart.
years.xp:
That was Andy Gill in NME, who called it 'bereft of even the most cursory contour of interest'. Sounds' Dave McCullough found it 'too priggish and conceited'. Trouser Press, in America, liked it.

Time has been kinder. Steve Albini called it 'a masterpiece'. The cover is Duane Michals's 1949 photograph Homage to Puvis de Chavannes.

years.h: A T. Rex cover, then up to Beggars Banquet
years.p: 'Telegram Sam' is the last 4AD single. Bauhaus outgrow the label and move to the parent company, the only 4AD band to make that planned step.

eras.title: Shoe factories and Ziggy
eras.text: On Beggars Banquet, Bauhaus added saxophone and keyboards, shot their own expressionist films, and finally had the hits. The biggest one was a Bowie song they'd started as a joke.

years.h: 'Kick in the Eye' is the first Beggars Banquet single
years.p: It reaches No. 59 in the UK and No. 29 on the US club chart. 'The Passion of Lovers' follows in June and gets to No. 56.

years.cap: Kevin Haskins, Peter Murphy, Daniel Ash and David J, c. 1981
years.h: Ash draws the cover of Mask
years.p: The second album brings in keyboards and saxophone and makes No. 30 in the UK. The title-track video is shot in an abandoned Victorian shoe factory in Northampton.
years.xp:
The video borrowed from German Expressionist film. 'We improvised around the loose idea of a ritualistic resurrection,' David J said, 'with Peter lain out like a corpse on a wooden slab.'

AllMusic's Ned Raggett called it 'arguably even better' than the debut, and it went silver in the UK.

years.h: Hugh Jones produces 'Spirit', and everybody agonizes
years.p: A rare single the band didn't produce themselves, with acoustic guitar and a bossa nova beat. It stalls at No. 42.
years.xp: 'There was so much agonizing over it more from the producer than us,' David J said.

q: we thought we'd do the opposite of what they'd expect
years.src: Wikipedia: Ziggy Stardust · Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Far Out: Bauhaus and
yt: Ziggy Stardust on Top of the Pops, 1982
years.h: A joke jam on 'Ziggy Stardust' becomes Bauhaus's biggest hit
years.p: Killing time at a BBC session, the band starts playing [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]]'s song as a tribute. Released as a single, it reaches No. 15 and puts them on Top of the Pops.
years.xp:
The press had been comparing them to Bowie for years. Ash's answer was to release a Bowie song.

The video was shot in the tunnels under Camden Market, staged as a fake gig with a full backline and fans. David J traced the whole band back to Bowie doing 'Starman' on Top of the Pops, which he called a profound turning point in their lives.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Sky · Wikipedia: Ziggy Stardust
years.h: The Sky's Gone Out goes to No. 3
years.p: A month at Rockfield in Wales produces the band's highest-charting album. First copies come with a free live album, Press the Eject and Give Me the Tape.
years.xp: It includes a cover of Brian Eno's 'Third Uncle'. Sources split on the peak: the album's Wikipedia article says No. 3, the 'Ziggy Stardust' article says No. 4.

eras.title: Burning from the inside
eras.text: A Hollywood film put Murphy's face on screens everywhere, and then pneumonia took him out of the studio. The other three made most of the fourth album without him, and the band played its last show before the record was even out.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: The Hunger · Wikipedia: Peter Murphy · Far Out: Bauhaus and
years.h: The Hunger opens on Bauhaus, and the camera stays on Murphy
years.p: Tony Scott's vampire film, with [[David Bowie|5441c29d-3602-4898-b1a1-b77fa23b8e50]] and Catherine Deneuve, starts in a nightclub with the band playing 'Bela Lugosi's Dead'. The final cut mostly shows Murphy.
years.xp:
With Murphy also the face of Maxell's 'Break the Sound Barrier' cassette ads, the attention bred resentment inside the band, according to Wikipedia's history.

The band shot the scene in March 1982, more than a year before the film came out, with Bowie on the same production.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: Burning from the Inside · Joel Gausten
years.h: Murphy gets double pneumonia; Ash and David J take the mic
years.p: With the singer sick through the Burning from the Inside sessions at Rockfield, the others write and record much of it themselves. Ash sings 'Slice of Life'; David J sings 'Who Killed Mr. Moonlight'.
years.xp:
David J described 'Who Killed Mr. Moonlight' as 'a surrealistic ballad inspired in part by the murder of John Lennon'.

The other three cut backing tracks without him, and the chemistry didn't recover. Ash later called those sessions 'the beginning of the end for Bauhaus'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · The Quietus · Wikipedia: Rest in Peace
years.h: Hammersmith Palais: David J walks off saying 'rest in peace'
years.p: Nobody announced it as the last show. After a long encore of early songs, the bass player leaves the stage with those words, and Bauhaus is done.
years.xp:
Murphy told the Quietus in 2011 he was 'burnt out, really', and frustrated 'because I was getting all the accolades and not the band.'

The show was recorded and came out in August 1992 on Nemo as Rest in Peace: The Final Concert.

years.src: Wikipedia: Burning from the Inside · Wikipedia: Bauhaus
years.h: Burning from the Inside comes out ten days after the band ends
years.p: It reaches No. 13; 'She's in Parties' makes No. 26 and gets the band a third Top of the Pops.
years.xp: David J said in 2015 that the title came from a night he and Ash were smoking hash in a car that caught fire from the inside.

eras.title: Three bands out of one
eras.text: Murphy went solo and later to Istanbul; the other three spun off Tones on Tail and then Love and Rockets, which got a Bauhaus offshoot higher on the American charts than the band ever went.

years.h: Tones on Tail makes Pop, then stops
years.p: Ash had started the side project in 1982 with Glenn Campling, a flatmate and former Bauhaus roadie, releasing an EP on 4AD. Haskins joins after the split; the album comes out in April 1984 and the band ends that year.
years.xp: The name comes from the calibration tones recorded on the tail of a reel-to-reel tape. They finished with a 12-date US tour in October, all in white.

years.h: Murphy forms Dalis Car with Mick Karn
years.p: The singer teams up with the bassist from [[Japan|697e7111-5630-4c77-83f3-39821bacc61a]] before starting a solo career.

years.cap: Daniel Ash with Love and Rockets, Oakland
years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: Love and Rockets
years.h: Ash and the Haskins brothers become Love and Rockets
years.p: After reunion rehearsals go nowhere without Murphy, the other three take a name from the Hernandez brothers' comic. Their first hit is a cover of the Temptations' 'Ball of Confusion'.

years.cap: Daniel Ash with Love and Rockets, 1989
years.h: 'So Alive' goes to No. 3 on the Billboard Hot 100
years.p: [[Love and Rockets|8cb3aa4a-3b4c-48b8-be0a-e57010fc1430]] land the biggest American hit any Bauhaus-related act has had, before or since.

years.h: Murphy's 'Cuts You Up' tops US Modern Rock for seven weeks
years.p: It's the lead single from Deep, which reaches No. 44 on the Billboard 200. Two years later Murphy moves to Istanbul with his Turkish wife, the choreographer Beyhan Foulkes.

eras.title: Undead, upside down
eras.text: The four reunited twice, first for a tour, then for a festival that ended up as a world tour, Nine Inch Nails support and a final album. They split before that album came out.

years.h: The Resurrection tour opens with Murphy on a TV screen
years.p: The first reunion is a tour only. The live album Gotham follows in 1999, with a studio cover of [[Dead Can Dance|ccda046a-2674-4f7d-97e6-f23d6c156432]]'s 'Severance'.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Far Out: Bauhaus at
years.h: At Coachella, Murphy descends upside down singing 'Bela Lugosi's Dead'
years.p: The reunion's first show, in Indio, California, opens with the singer lowered to the stage head first. A North American and European tour follows through February 2006.
years.xp: It was the four's first show together since 1998, on a bill with Weezer and Gang of Four. After the opener they played 'She's in Parties', 'Dark Entries' and 'Silent Hedges'.

years.h: Bauhaus opens for Nine Inch Nails
years.p: [[Nine Inch Nails|b7ffd2af-418f-4be2-bdd1-22f8b48613da]] were among the bands that grew up on them. On the 2005–06 shows Bauhaus also cover [[Joy Division|9a58fda3-f4ed-4080-a3a5-f457aac9fcdd]]'s 'Transmission'.

years.big: 'He just spits rose petals in our faces.'
years.src: Wikipedia: Go Away White · Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Joel Gausten
years.h: Go Away White is the last album, and there's no tour
years.p: Recorded in 18 days in 2006 at Zircon Skye in Ojai, California, and released on Cooking Vinyl after the band had split again.
years.xp:
'We were getting along really well, but there was an incident that occurred,' Haskins said. 'Some of us just felt that we didn't want to carry on.'

David J says it nearly ended the sessions until Murphy came in and spat rose petals at them: 'It just cut through everything.' Pitchfork called the album a 'surprisingly true-to-form swan song'.

'We went in with hardly any material, just some lyrics,' David J said of the 2006 sessions, which covered writing, recording and mixing in about three weeks. [[Trent Reznor|bc880664-6751-4998-984d-ebdbff15d229]] heard it and told them to put it out as it was: 'I love this record!' Ash, for his part: 'I don't ever listen to that album.'

eras.title: One more time at the Palladium
eras.text: The members toured in pairs for a few years: Ash and Haskins as Poptone, Murphy and David J doing the first album in full. Then all four came back for the Hollywood Palladium, a new single and a tour that ended early.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: Daniel Ash · Wikipedia: David J
years.h: Ash and Haskins start Poptone with Haskins's daughter on bass
years.p: Diva Dompé plays bass in a set of Bauhaus, Tones on Tail and Love and Rockets songs. In 2018 Murphy and David J tour the 40th anniversary, playing In the Flat Field in full.

years.h: Murphy has a heart attack during a New York residency
years.p: He's taken from (Le) Poisson Rouge for an angioplasty, gets two stents, and recovers.

years.cap: Bauhaus at the Hollywood Palladium, November 4, 2019
years.h: All four originals at the Hollywood Palladium, the first time in 13 years
years.p: Three shows at the 4,000-seat Los Angeles hall: November 3 and 4, and December 1.

years.cap: SF Masonic Auditorium, San Francisco, May 2022
years.h: 'Drink the New Wine', recorded apart
years.p: The first new song in 14 years is made separately during the COVID-19 lockdown, each member adding a part in the exquisite corpse method.

years.h: Murphy enters rehab; the East Coast dates are cancelled
years.p: The European and West Coast legs of the tour had gone ahead.

years.src: Wikipedia: Bauhaus · Wikipedia: Love and Rockets
years.h: Ash confirms Bauhaus is over; Love and Rockets return
years.p: On May 20 Love and Rockets play the Cruel World festival in Pasadena, their first show in 15 years.
